editorial.headline: Leather Wholesale Is Nationally Open—But Blocked for PMA in Bali
editorial.standfirst: Wholesale trade in leather and imitation leather is nationally open to full foreign ownership, yet Bali’s permanent risk-based moratorium blocks PMA registration today.
editorial.body:
This activity is wholesale trade in leather and imitation leather: the commercial layer that moves these materials through the market rather than presenting them as a finished consumer proposition. Its scope is deliberately material-specific, centred on leather and its imitation counterparts, and its character is wholesale. That distinction gives the activity its practical shape: it concerns the business of supplying these materials at scale.

The registration field is broad in business size. It is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar enterprises, so the classification does not reserve the activity for one particular commercial scale. Nationally, it is also TERBUKA to foreign investment, with a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In plain terms, the national framework allows full foreign ownership for this activity.

Bali is where the position changes decisively. A foreign investor cannot register this activity in Bali today. At the Besar scale, OSS risk is classified as Rendah or Menengah-Rendah across every scope, placing it within Bali’s moratorium. The provincial rule blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI activities for PMA on an island-wide, permanent basis; the recorded basis identifies the moratorium as taking effect in May 2026.

This is therefore not a case for softening the message with a national headline alone. Full foreign ownership remains the national ceiling, but that ceiling does not create a Bali registration route where the provincial PMA block applies. Founders assessing this activity should keep those two layers separate: nationally open, but unavailable for PMA registration in Bali under the stated risk-based moratorium.
